name: The Bald Cypress of Parc Borely

location.address: Parc Borely, near the lake, Avenue du Prado / Avenue Clot-Bey, 13008 Marseille

verified_sources: OSM natural=tree node 2365945745, species=Taxodium distichum, at 43.260329,5.3835936 (reverse-geocodes to Avenue Clot-Bey / Grand Saint-Giniez, immediately beside Parc Borely, matching the Direction des Parcs et Jardins own address of 48 avenue Clot-Bey)
access: Free, public park, open daily (typically 6:30am-8:30/9:30pm depending on season)
transport: Tram T3 or Bus, Rond-Point du Prado stop, then short walk; Parc Borely metro is not direct, nearest is Castellane then tram
verify_notes: Bald cypress (Taxodium distichum, cypres chauve or cypres de Louisiane) growing beside the lake in Parc Borely, Marseille 8e. Distinctive aerial roots (pneumatophores) rise from the ground around the trunk, a Louisiana swamp adaptation for waterlogged soil, and are the tree's main visual draw. Two independent OSM tree nodes tag Taxodium distichum right beside the lake at 43.2603/5.3836 and 43.2600/5.3828, both reverse-geocoding to ground immediately adjacent to Parc Borely (Avenue Clot-Bey, Grand Saint-Giniez/Bonneveine), matching the park's own administrative address. Species introduced to France mid-18th century; provence7.com states this specimen was labelled Arbre remarquable by the A.R.B.R.E.S. association in 2009, but that is a SINGLE source for the label claim and could not be independently confirmed (arbres.org label-validation lists checked only cover 2024 batches; no dedicated arbres.org fiche for this tree was found). FLAGGED for that reason: species and existence are corroborated by multiple independent sources, but the 2009 label date rests on one source only. No age or girth is documented anywhere found; do not use the species' native-range lifespan potential (600-1200 years, quoted by provence7.com) as an age estimate for this individual specimen, that figure describes what the species CAN reach in its native swamp habitat, not this tree's actual age, and repeating it would be a bridge claim. Ask the reader for a trunk girth if anyone has one.

name: The Southern Magnolia of Parc Borely

location.address: Parc Borely, 8th arrondissement, Marseille (exact tree within the park not pinpointed)

transport: Tram T3 or bus, Rond-Point du Prado stop, then short walk
verify_notes: Southern Magnolia (Magnolia grandiflora) at Parc Borely, Marseille 8e. jardinsdefrance.org (Societe Nationale d Horticulture de France), in a roundup of exceptional Magnolia grandiflora specimens across France by trunk girth and crown height, lists it exactly as: "Marseille, Parc Borely, plante en 1929 : 2,22 m/20 m" (2.22m circumference measured at 1m above ground, 20m crown height). CAUTION: an earlier WebSearch AI summary of the same page mis-attributed a different row in that same list (Grasse, planted 1956, 2.7m/18m) to Marseille; the figures used here were confirmed by fetching and reading the raw page text directly, per the search-summary-is-a-lead-never-a-source rule. graines-et-plantes.com independently corroborates a Magnolia grandiflora as a standout, remarkable specimen with ivory-coloured flowers in the park, without giving measurements. Documented planting date (1929) is the basis for the age figure, not a growth-rate estimate; roughly 95-97 years old as of 2026. LOCATION_PRECISION IS APPROXIMATE: neither source gives which part of the 17-hectare park it stands in. One Magnolia grandiflora is tagged as an OSM natural=tree node (id 2365945739) at 43.2597652,5.383882, inside/immediately adjacent to Parc Borely near the same spot as the bald cypresses (mrs_001), but this is supporting evidence only, not proof it is the same 1929 specimen, since ordinary magnolias also grow in the park. A future pass should look for the park s own tree-trail signage (a 1995 pedagogical circuit exists per marseille-autrement.fr, walking about twenty remarkable trees) to pin the exact spot.

name: The Plane Tree of Place des Augustines

location.address: Place des Augustines, Le Panier, 13002 Marseille

verified_sources: OSM natural=tree node 1346333315 at 43.2973337,5.3686195, tagged denotation=natural_monument, species=Platanus hispanica, reverse-geocoding to Place des Augustines, Le Panier, Marseille 2e
access: Free, standing in a public square in Le Panier, always visible/accessible
transport: Metro line 1 or 2, Vieux-Port or Colbert stop, short walk into Le Panier
verify_notes: A large London Plane (Platanus x hispanica/acerifolia) standing in Place des Augustines, the small square at the heart of Le Panier, Marseille s oldest quarter, on the site of a former Ursuline (1636) then Augustine (1748) convent. Multiple independent tourism/lifestyle sources describe it consistently as the dominant, shading feature of the square: love-spots.com calls it "the great plane tree"; croquisurbains.fr notes "son bar du platane d une certaine epoque aussi" (a bar named for the plane tree, itself of some age); the restaurant La Table d Augustine, which opened on the square in 2023 and sits directly beneath it, describes it on its own site as "le plus vieux platane du centre-ville, temoin silencieux des siecles passes" (the oldest plane tree in the city centre, silent witness to centuries past). FLAGGED because the only source giving an age figure at all is the restaurant s own promotional copy (an interested party, and "oldest in the city centre" is an unverified superlative); other sources agree only that it is old and large, not by how much. Using the vague plural ("centuries", "siecles passes") rather than sharpening to a number, per the rule against turning a vague source into a precise one. OSM tags a single London Plane node right at this square s coordinates with denotation=natural_monument, a legal/heritage-protection style tag, which is corroborating but crowd-sourced and not itself verified against a French official register. No canker-stain (Ceratocystis platani) news or dieback reports found for this specific tree; the restaurant opening beneath it in 2023 and the square s tourism write-ups being current implies the tree is alive and healthy as of recently, though no dated photo/observation was directly viewed. Ask a reader for a trunk girth or a more precise planting record if anyone in Le Panier has one.
